acceptance: Tuned TPC-H/TPC-DS runs with partitioning on a date column load successfully on a local PostgreSQL container and the tables are partitioned with a DEFAULT partition.
Partitioning is skipped and recorded as dropped with a reason when primary or unique keys are requested.
Registry postgresql PARTITIONING entry flipped to a rendered mechanism; registry parity, snapshot and fake-driver execution tests pass.
context: Owner-approved 2026-10-17 (coordinator relay of owner decision). Clustering/sorting half ships under tuning-render-layout-postgres-family-20261001.
description: Partitioning half of tuning-render-layout-postgres-family-20261001, split by owner decision 2026-10-17. PostgreSQLDDLGenerator's RANGE partitions are hardcoded to yearly 2020-2026 children while TPC-H/TPC-DS dates fall in 1992-2003, so rendering them as-is fails every load. Change: derive RANGE partition bounds from the benchmark's date domain, always add a DEFAULT partition, and skip partitioning (recording it as dropped with a reason) when primary or unique keys are requested, because PostgreSQL requires those keys to include the partition column. Flip the postgresql PARTITIONING registry entry once execution renders it, with a snapshot test (adapter output equals generator output), a fake-driver execution test, and a local Postgres container run. Postgres-compatible variants keep their own entries.
